subject: Post-demo: EmberPay integration — payload serialization causing 5xxs
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Gupta <ava.gupta@emberpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: EmberPay integration — payload serialization causing 5xxs

Hi Ava — great demo earlier, thanks again. Quick recap and immediate asks so we can unblock your integration:

Recap
- You shipped the SDK integration and started sending structured tool-calling requests + embeddings for transaction enrichment.
- On your side you started seeing intermittent 5xx responses from the Redwood hosted endpoint after the change to the new payload shape.

Immediate asks
1) Can you share a representative request payload and the corresponding server log lines for one of the 5xx responses? (attach as emberpay_sample_payload.json and emberpay_server_logs.txt if convenient)
2) Which SDK + version are you using? If it’s the browser SDK, confirm whether you’re setting content-type explicitly.
3) Can you tell us whether you see 5xxs on all models/endpoints or just the reranker/structured route?

Proposed next steps
- If you can share a minimal failing payload + a reproducible request-id, we’ll try to repro in our staging and identify whether this is a serialization mismatch or an edge runtime issue.
- Tentative plan: triage today, repro + hotfix tomorrow, canary deploy and monitor for 24h.

I’ve attached a sample payload format we typically use for tool-calls to show expected shapes (emberpay_sample_payload.json).

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: emberpay_sample_payload.json (application/json)

-----Original message attached by EmberPay (below)-----

From: Ava Gupta <ava.gupta@emberpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: EmberPay SRE <sre@emberpay.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberPay integration — payload serialization causing 5xxs

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick follow-up.

We started seeing the 5xxs shortly after switching to a nested inputs array for tool calls and adding a serialized JSON string into tool_call.args (we pass an object but the SDK on our side stringifies it before sending). Example: tool_call.args = JSON.stringify({ merchant_id: 123, items: [...] })

Attached are our server logs and a raw captured request (emberpay_server_logs.txt). The error from our side shows "500 Internal Server Error" and the Redwood response includes a short error id: rwd-5xx-0901 (copied from logs).

A couple details:
- SDK: emberpay/redwood-js v0.9.1 (browser)
- Auth: long-lived API key in a proxy layer (no session-based auth)
- We see the 5xxs against the structured tool-calling route only, not plain text generation.

Open to a joint engineering session if helpful.

— Ava
Ava Gupta
Head of Integrations | EmberPay
ava.gupta@emberpay.com

Attachments: emberpay_server_logs.txt (text/plain)

-----Internal triage (internal recipients only)-----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberPay integration — initial findings

Quick triage notes after reproducing locally with the sample payload Ava shared:

What I reproduced
- Using the sample payload where tool_call.args is a JSON-encoded string I get a 500 from the structured-execution runtime after ~18s.
- Error trace points to our schema validation step expecting an object for tool_call.args (we validate shape and then run kernels). If the field is a string we attempt a JSON.parse path that currently assumes well-formed object and can throw on certain escaped sequences.

Probable root cause
- Double-encoding: EmberPay’s SDK is stringifying an object before sending. Our runtime expects a native object for tool_call.args (or a top-level string for free text). The mismatch leads to a parsing edge case that can throw and bubble up as a 500.

Mitigations / next steps
1) Short-term workaround: ask EmberPay to stop stringifying tool_call.args; send a proper JSON object in the request. That fixes repro immediately.
2) Medium-term (our side): make schema validation more defensive — if tool_call.args is a string try a safe JSON.parse with try/catch and return 4xx with a clear error (instead of 5xx). I can open a PR to change the validation behavior.
3) Increase timeout on the structured route in staging from 15s to 45s while we patch, to avoid the runtime hitting hard timeouts during parsing under certain payload sizes.

Sample log snippet (local repro):
"2026-08-30T09:02:12Z ERROR structured-exec: schema-validation failed: unhandled exception in parse_path at /srv/runtime/exec.go:402 stack=... rwd-5xx-0901"
I’ll draft a minimal repro script and a patch for defensive parsing today. If we want to push a hotfix tomorrow I can take that on.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

-----External response and plan summary-----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Gupta <ava.gupta@emberpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, EmberPay SRE <sre@emberpay.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 18:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberPay integration — payload serialization causing 5xxs

Hi Ava, thanks for the logs and for the quick context. We reproduced the error and have a clear next-step plan:

What we found
- Root cause: SDK on your side is stringifying tool_call.args. Our structured execution expects a JSON object in tool_call.args; when we try to parse a nested string we hit an unhandled edge case that results in a 500.

Immediate workaround (you can deploy this now)
- Send tool_call.args as a native JSON object (do not JSON.stringify before sending). This is the fastest way to stop the 5xxs and should immediately remove the error from your end.

Our actions (timeline)
- Today (Aug 30): Ben opened a defensive-parsing PR to return a 400 with a clear error message if parsing fails instead of throwing 500.
- Tomorrow (Aug 31 morning): We’ll deploy the fix to staging and run a short smoke test with your sample payloads.
- Sept 1: Can run a joint canary with you and monitor for 24 hours. Proposed time: 2026-09-01 10:00 AM PT for a 30–45 minute check-in (engineering + SRE). Please confirm if that works for your team.

Temporary tuning
- We’ll increase the structured-route timeout in staging to 45s while we test. No change needed on your side for this step.

Next steps for EmberPay
1) If possible, push the minor SDK change to stop stringifying tool_call.args. If you want, we can supply a 1-line patch for emberpay/redwood-js v0.9.1.
2) Confirm availability for the Sept 1 canary call.

If you prefer we can schedule an engineering pairing session tonight to walk through the repro. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the plan above and loop you in on the staging results.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you fully unblocked.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-emberpay-integration (shared repro + logs)
